s.en: Merges two or more capture files into one

syn: mergecap [ -a ] [ -F <file format> ] [ -I <IDB merge mode> ] [ -s <snaplen> ] [ -V ] -w <outfile>|- <infile> [<infile> ...] ⏎ mergecap -h|--help ⏎ mergecap -v|--version

o.en: Causes the frame timestamps to be ignored, writing all packets from the first input file followed by all packets from the second input file. By default, when -a is not specified, the contents of the input files are merged in chronological order based on each frame’s timestamp.

<file format> Sets the file format of the output capture file. Mergecap can write the file in several formats; mergecap -F provides a list of the available output formats. By default this is the pcapng format. Print the version number and options and exit.

<IDB merge mode> Sets the Interface Description Block (IDB) merge mode to use during merging. mergecap -I provides a list of the available IDB merge modes. Every input file has one or more IDBs, which describe the interface(s) the capture was performed on originally. This includes encapsulation type, interface name, etc.

<snaplen> Sets the snapshot length to use when writing the data. If the -s flag is used to specify a snapshot length, frames in the input file with more captured data than the specified snapshot length will have only the amount of data specified by the snapshot length written to the output file.
Causes mergecap to print a number of messages while it’s working.

<outfile>|- Sets the output filename. If the name is '-', stdout will be used. If the --compress option is not given, then the filename extension is used to deduce the desired compression method, if any; e.g., if the name has the extension '.gz', then the output file is compressed to a gzip archive. This setting is mandatory.

Compress the output file using the type compression format. --compress with no argument provides a list of the compression formats supported for writing. The type given takes precedence over the extension of outfile.

Set the active log level. Supported levels in lowest to highest order are "noisy", "debug", "info", "message", "warning", "critical", and "error". Messages at each level and higher will be printed, for example "warning" prints "warning", "critical", and "error" messages and "noisy" prints all messages.
Abort the program if any messages are logged at the specified level or higher. For example, "warning" aborts on any "warning", "critical", or "error" messages.
Only print messages for the specified log domains, e.g. "GUI,Epan,sshdump". List of domains must be comma-separated. Can be negated with "!" as the first character (inverts the match).
Force the specified domains to log at the "debug" level. List of domains must be comma-separated. Can be negated with "!" as the first character (inverts the match).
Force the specified domains to log at the "noisy" level. List of domains must be comma-separated. Can be negated with "!" as the first character (inverts the match).
Abort the program if any messages are logged for the specified log domains. List of domains must be comma-separated.
Write log messages and stderr output to the specified file.
